pages.text: Something Is Here
pages.subtext: Mira and Pip's Nothing Hunt
pages.alt: Mira and Pip hold a curling treasure map marked with a question symbol. Around them are a blue box, a bell, a blank card, a curtain and five bright clue stars from the story game.

pages.subtext: Play, spot, wonder and check with a grown-up.
pages.alt: An open book sits beside a round stamp reading Review 1.1.0 and a small magnifying glass.

pages.text:
Mira found a mystery map.

FIND NOTHING, it said.
pages.subtext: Pip flapped his wings. 'A treasure hunt!'
pages.alt: Mira stands beside a large map headed FIND NOTHING while Pip flaps at its other side. Five empty star spaces show that five clues are waiting.

pages.text:
Spot a clue.
Say what you notice.
Turn the page to check.
pages.subtext: Keep every surprise. That is how detectives learn.
pages.alt: Three large game cards show the text and symbols EYE for spot, a question mark for say and OK for check. Pip waits beside the first card.

pages.text:
What is here in Mira's room?

Can you spot five things?
pages.subtext: Point, name, sign or make a sound for each one.
pages.alt: A playful room contains Mira, Pip, a blue box, a yellow bell, a striped rug, a lamp, a question card and a tiny toy star partly peeking from behind the box.

pages.text:
Mira is here. Pip is here.
The box, bell and rug are here too.
pages.subtext: Did you find different things? They count as clues too.
pages.alt: The same room returns with five numbered loops around Mira, Pip, the blue box, yellow bell and striped rug. A small star still peeks out as an extra thing to spot.

pages.text:
Mira opened the box.
No toy was inside.

Did she find nothing?
pages.subtext: Look closely before you decide.
pages.alt: Mira and Pip stand beside an open blue box with no toy inside. The box, its raised lid and empty pale-blue interior are clearly visible.

pages.text:
The toy was not inside.
But the box was here.
Looking was happening.
pages.subtext: Empty inside is not the same as no thing shown.
pages.alt: The open box is labelled BOX HERE, the empty inside is labelled NO TOY INSIDE, and a dotted gaze line from Mira is labelled LOOKING.

pages.text:
EMPTY tells us what is missing from a container.

The container can still be here.
pages.subtext: Pip sticks the first star on the map.
pages.alt: Pip places the first gold star onto the map. A small empty blue box remains visible beside the star.

pages.text:
Mira waited.
The bell did not ring.

What DID happen?
pages.subtext: Cup your hand by your ear and listen with Mira.
pages.alt: Mira and Pip listen beside a yellow bell that is not moving. A short three-dot listening trail invites the child to pause.

pages.text:
No ring happened.
Mira listened.
Pip waited.
The bell stayed still.
pages.subtext: Can you spot all three happenings in the picture?
pages.alt: Three numbered markers identify Mira listening, Pip waiting and the bell staying still. Curved sound lines are crossed out only beside the bell.

pages.text:
Pip found a blank card.

'Nothing!' he chirped.

What can YOU spot?
pages.subtext: There are four clues before you turn the page.
pages.alt: A large blank cream card lies on a table. Its four spot-able clues are the card itself, its dark edge, Pip's orange feather resting on it and Mira's magnifying glass above it.

pages.text:
The card was here.
Its edge was here.
A feather and a magnifying glass were here.
pages.subtext: Blank means no mark on the card. It does not make the card disappear.
pages.alt: The blank card scene returns with numbered arrows pointing to the card, edge, orange feather and magnifying glass.

pages.text:
A word is hiding in this busy picture.

Can you find NOTHING?
pages.subtext: Look across the blocks from left to right.
pages.alt: Seven coloured letter blocks appear among four outline stars. Reading the blocks from left to right reveals N O T H I N G.

pages.text:
You found the word NOTHING.

The word is something we can see and read.
pages.subtext: A name does not turn into the thing it names.
pages.alt: Seven letter blocks spelling NOTHING are collected in a row inside a bright outline. Mira points to the blocks while Pip holds a check card.

pages.text:
Mira hid every toy behind a curtain.

Did the room become nothing?
pages.subtext: Spot what stayed in the picture.
pages.alt: A purple curtain hides a pile of toys. Mira, Pip, the curtain, the floor and two toy-shaped bumps behind the fabric remain visible.

pages.text:
The toys were hidden.
The curtain was here.
Mira and Pip were still playing.
pages.subtext: Hidden from one view is not no thing shown.
pages.alt: The curtain scene returns with labels for CURTAIN and TOYS HIDDEN. Mira and Pip remain visible on opposite sides, and two toy-shaped bumps remain below the curtain.

pages.text:
Five clue stars made the map POP open.

Two mystery doors appeared.
pages.subtext: 'One last level,' said Mira.
pages.alt: The map opens into a game board with five gold stars and two doors. Door A shows a hand holding a card; Door B has an open frame with no card supplied.

pages.text:
Door A says: 'Here is my nothing.'
Door B gives no example.

Which door can Mira check?
pages.subtext: Follow each path with your finger.
pages.alt: Door A contains a presented star card. Door B contains a dashed empty frame and supplies no card. Large letters A and B distinguish the doors as well as colour.

pages.text:
Door A gives Mira an example.
Giving it is happening.
The card is here.
pages.subtext: So Door A has shown something—not nothing.
pages.alt: Door A is open and an arrow carries its star card toward Mira. Three numbered markers identify the card, the handover and Mira's inspection.

pages.text:
Door B gives no example.
There is nothing for Mira to point to or check.
pages.subtext: We do not pretend a secret example was given.
pages.alt: Mira stands beside Door B's dashed empty frame. A simple sign says NO EXAMPLE GIVEN; no card or hidden object appears in the frame.

pages.text:
Can you draw nothing on a card?

Try—or choose not to draw.
pages.subtext: Then turn the page. Both choices are allowed.
pages.alt: A blank drawing card and chunky crayon sit between two choice arrows: MAKE A MARK and MAKE NO MARK. Mira waits without choosing for the child.

pages.text:
Made a mark? The mark is here.
Made no mark? The card is still here.
pages.subtext: Either way, no drawn example of nothing appeared.
pages.alt: Two cards sit side by side. One has a spiral mark labelled MARK HERE; the other stays blank and is labelled CARD HERE. Both rest inside check outlines.

pages.text:
Show an example—and the showing is something.
Show no example—and there is no example to use.
pages.subtext: Every level of the Nothing Hunt gave the same clue.
pages.alt: Mira stands beside a detective board. A presented star card leads by a solid green line to SOMETHING, while a dashed empty frame leads to NO EXAMPLE TO USE.

pages.text: There is no nothing.
pages.subtext: Mira and Pip found the starting clue of Smithian Fold Theory.
pages.alt: A brown treasure chest with a raised lid reveals a gold card reading THERE IS NO NOTHING. Mira and Pip stand beside all five collected clue stars.

pages.text:
Our game checks what can be shown, said, drawn or recorded.

It does not make up things no one can show.
pages.subtext: Good detectives say where their rule stops.
pages.alt: A green game mat contains four picture tokens for show, say, draw and record. Beyond its rope boundary is an unmarked area carrying no invented example.

pages.text:
Find four clues:
an empty box, a still bell, a blank card and a hidden toy.
pages.subtext: For each clue, say what is here and what did not happen or appear.
pages.alt: One large search scene contains an open empty box, a still yellow bell, a blank card and a toy partly hidden by a curtain, plus Mira, Pip and five harmless decoy shapes.

pages.text:
Box here—no toy inside.
Bell here—no ring.
Card here—no mark.
Curtain here—toy hidden.
pages.subtext: You kept each missing thing separate from what was present.
pages.alt: The final search scene returns with four numbered loops around the empty box, still bell, blank card and curtain hiding the toy. Each loop has a matching picture answer.

pages.text:
Which cards show something to check?
Which card gives no example?
pages.subtext: Move your finger from each picture to a basket.
pages.alt: Four picture cards show an empty box, a still bell, a blank page and a dashed NO EXAMPLE GIVEN frame. Two baskets are labelled SOMETHING TO CHECK and NO EXAMPLE GIVEN.

pages.text:
Box, bell and card: something to check.
No example given: no example to use.
pages.subtext: The words empty, still and blank did not erase the things.
pages.alt: The empty box, still bell and blank-card pictures sit in the SOMETHING TO CHECK basket. Only the dashed no-example frame sits beside the NO EXAMPLE GIVEN basket.

pages.text:
I spotted.
I wondered.
I checked.
I kept the surprises.
pages.subtext: Add your name, mark or sticker with a grown-up.
pages.alt: Mira and Pip hold a large detective certificate with spaces for a child's name or mark and an optional sticker. Five clue stars form a border.

pages.text:
The first mystery is solved.

But the treasure is ONE whole...
pages.subtext: Next: One Whole, Many Parts
pages.alt: Mira and Pip follow the map toward one large golden circle made from several visible fitting pieces, previewing the next book.
